title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The prose claims Dynam3D 'achieves modest improvements of approximately 1-2% in navigation success rate (SR)' on R2R-CE relative to g3D-LF/Uni-NaVid and 'outperforming NaVid by approximately 3-5% in Success Rate (SR) on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE'. Table 1 shows R2R-CE Val SR 52.9 vs g3D-LF 47.2 (+5.7 pp) and vs Uni-NaVid 47.0 (+5.9 pp), and Test SR 51.4 vs g3D-LF 46.3 (+5.1 pp). Table 2 shows REVERIE-CE Val SR 40.1 vs NaVid 26.6 (+13.5 pp) and NavRAG-CE Val SR 24.7 vs NaVid 19.4 (+5.3 pp). No metric in either table produces a 1-2% R2R-CE gain, and the REVERIE-CE gain is +13.5 points, roughly 3-4x the claimed 3-5%. The stated improvement ranges are mathematically inconsistent with the table deltas, and the mismatch is material to the paper's headline performance claim.

The Robustness-to-Noise text states 'we perform ablation by degrading the quality of 3D instance and zone embeddings through feature dropout and spatial jitter to evaluate sensitivity. Table 7 shows that while navigation success rate (SR) decreases with noise addition, it degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised.' However, Table 7 as printed contains only four rows — no noise, SLAM noise only, depth noise only, SLAM+depth noise — i.e., exclusively SLAM and depth noise conditions. There are NO feature-dropout or spatial-jitter representation-degradation rows, so the cited table does not support the claim that representation-quality degradation hurts more than noise. The table supports only 'SR decreases with noise addition' (52.9 -> 50.9 for combined noise), not the stronger representation-fidelity conclusion the text attributes to it.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification (lenient strictness, threshold 0.30) of 'Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation' (cs.CV; 34 snippets: 16 sections, 7 equations, 7 tables, 4 figures). Triage escalated 23 snippets (uncertainty >= 0.30) to specialist verifiers: 7 equations to math, 12 numeric snippets to statistical (5 sections + 7 tables), 2 sections to text, 2 sections to citation; a full cross-section consistency pass was also run. Two findings passed the confidence filters (statistical >= 0.7, text >= 0.8): (1) Section 4.1 prose understates the table-reported SR gains — the text claims ~1-2% improvement over g3D-LF/Uni-NaVid on R2R-CE and ~3-5% over NaVid on REVERIE-CE/NavRAG-CE, whereas Tables 1-2 show +5.7/+5.9 percentage points on R2R-CE and +13.5/+5.3 points on REVERIE-CE/NavRAG-CE, a ~3-4x discrepancy (confidence 0.9). (2) Section 4.6 attributes to Table 7 a feature-dropout/spatial-jitter representation-quality ablation ('degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised') that Table 7 does not contain — the table covers only SLAM and depth noise (confidence 0.85). All equations (Eqs 1-7) were verified mathematically consistent (pinhole projection, frustum culling, instance encoder, segmentation and contrastive/subspace-distillation losses); all seven tables satisfy internal metric constraints (OSR >= SR, SPL <= SR, percentages in [0,100], integer-consistent with N=20 real-world cases); the computational-cost arithmetic sums correctly (455 = 83+315+57; 649 = 83+540+26); the ablation ordering (Patch > Instance > Zone) and the '~10%'/'~15%' drop characterizations match Table 6; the abstract/conclusion/results are mutually consistent (all use the moderate 'competitive performance' framing), with no macro-level contradictions; and the citation spot-checks found all references real with matching attributions and the GitHub code repo confirmed. Both flagged findings are conservative-direction text-table reporting inconsistencies rather than result-inflating fraud, but they are material to the paper's headline performance claims and the robustness analysis, so the paper is judged NEEDS_CORRECTION.
